name: St. Jakob in Haus
kurzbeschreibung: Peaceful mountain village in the Pillerseetal with the historic church and stunning hikes around Pillersee.
beschreibung:
St. Jakob in Haus lies at 810 metres above sea level in the district of Kitzbühel, set within the region around the Pillersee. The village has around 800 inhabitants and is one of the quieter municipalities in the Kitzbüheler Alpen. The name refers to the Apostle James, who also shapes the parish church of the village – a late Gothic building that has formed the centre of village life for centuries.

The surroundings invite you to hike and linger. Directly from the village centre, paths lead up to the Buchensteinwand and onward into the Loferer Steinberge, where mountain hikers and families alike find suitable tours. An insider tip is the Jaufenburg castle ruins high above the village, from which the view opens far into the Pillerseetal. Culturally interesting: The so-called Jauferbuch, one of the oldest testimonies of medieval German utilitarian poetry, is said to have originated here in the 12th century – a rare piece of the literary history of Tirol.

In winter, St. Jakob in Haus lies directly on the Pillersee-Tal-Abfahrt of the Buchensteinwand ski area; in summer, the Pillersee swimming lake, just a few kilometres away, beckons. text:
Overview

St. Jakob in Haus is situated at an elevation of 855 meters in the sunny high-altitude Pillerseetal valley in the Kitzbühel district, resting at the western base of Mount Buchensteinwand (1,456 m). Framed by the rolling peaks of the Kitzbühel Alps to the south and the dramatic limestone walls of the Loferer and Leoganger Steinberge to the northeast, it is the smallest municipality in the Kitzbühel district, home to approximately 800 residents. St. Jakob in Haus preserves the tranquil, unspoiled ambience of a traditional Tyrolean village: located away from through traffic, it combines pastoral calm with major family attractions, including the world’s largest accessible summit cross—the Jakobskreuz—and the Familienland Pillersee theme park.

History

The settlement was first recorded in 1308 as zue sant Jacob hintz Haus under the authority of the Benedictine abbey of Rott am Inn. The village grew as a staging post along the Tyrolean Way of Saint James. The parish church of Saint James the Greater dates back to the 13th century. In February 1689, a catastrophic avalanche destroyed the Gothic nave; the church was rebuilt that same year around its surviving choir and tower, consecrated in September 1689 with rich Baroque interior fittings crafted by Kufstein master sculptor Georg Faistenberger. Originally a chapelry of St. Ulrich am Pillersee, it gained independent parish status in 1891. In 2014, the imposing Jakobskreuz cross was consecrated atop the Buchensteinwand as a modern architectural tribute to regional pilgrimage.

Getting there

St. Jakob in Haus is easily reached by road and rail. By car from Germany or Innsbruck, exit the A12 motorway at Wörgl-Ost and follow federal highway B178 via St. Johann in Tirol, turning onto the B164 towards Fieberbrunn before taking the L234 Pillersee road directly into the village. Rail travelers alight at the express railway station in St. Johann in Tirol or at Fieberbrunn station on the Salzburg-Tyrol line. VVT regional bus line 8302 connects both stations with St. Jakob in Haus throughout the day, providing free bus transit for guests holding the regional guest card.

Tips

Ascend the Buchensteinwand chairlift to visit the 29.6-meter-high Jakobskreuz, the world’s largest walk-in summit cross, featuring elevator access, heated exhibition rooms, and multiple open-air platforms commanding panoramic views stretching from the Wilder Kaiser to the Grossglockner. In winter, the mountain operates as a relaxed family ski area with dedicated children's facilities. In summer, families flock to the Erlebnispark Familienland Pillersee, home to Austria's highest family roller coaster Big Bang, water rides, and an indoor Dead Sea salt cave for respiratory wellness. Walking through the Baroque parish church or exploring the Pillersee cycling trails rounds out a memorable visit.
